name: Holographic Extreme Cache
author: Holographic

sections.description:
Holographic Extreme Cache gives WordPress sites a faster, cleaner caching layer with safe defaults and practical performance tools.

It includes advanced static page caching, intelligent cache clearing, WooCommerce-safe exclusions, preload support, HTML minification, WordPress emoji disabling, browser cache helper rules, new-upload WebP image conversion where supported, homepage speed testing and cache diagnostics.

Built for real WordPress sites, it helps pages load faster while avoiding risky one-size-fits-all optimisation. Smart clearing keeps cached content fresher, WooCommerce-safe rules protect dynamic shop pages, optional WebP conversion helps newly uploaded images load more efficiently, and built-in diagnostics make performance easier to trust.

Features

  • Static HTML page caching.
  • PHP fallback cache delivery.
  • advanced-cache.php drop-in support.
  • Optional Apache rewrite helper rules.
  • Manual clear cache button.
  • Admin bar cache clearing.
  • Automatic cache clearing when content changes.
  • Basic smart purge for posts, pages, archives, taxonomy archives, authors and homepage.
  • Cache lifetime control.
  • Basic preload for homepage, recent posts and recent pages.
  • Combined cache and preload controls for simpler setup.
  • Safe default exclusions.
  • WooCommerce cart, checkout and account exclusions.
  • Logged-in user bypass by default, with an advanced option for sites that understand the risks.
  • POST, AJAX, REST, preview and unsafe query string bypass.
  • Cache size and cached page count.
  • Last purge and last preload time.
  • Basic cache health check.
  • Other caching plugin conflict detection.
  • Debug response headers.
  • Strong cached HTML and inline CSS minification.
  • Disable WordPress emoji files option.
  • Browser cache helper.
  • Gzip and Brotli detection.
  • Optional WebP conversion for newly uploaded JPEG and PNG images where supported by the server.
  • Safe WebP fallback handling so original images remain available.
  • Images tab showing server WebP support and image conversion settings.
  • Setup checklist to help site owners finish the main cache setup steps.
  • Setup tab with one-click WP_CACHE handling where wp-config.php is writable.
  • Simple homepage speed test for cache-off and cache-on comparison with expandable diagnostics.
  • Safe and Balanced modes.
  • Optional uninstall cleanup.

Privacy

Holographic Extreme Cache does not collect analytics, does not track visitors and does not send site data to a third-party service.

The plugin stores cache files, configuration helper files, generated WebP image files and optional log files inside the WordPress uploads directory. Logging is off by default.

Uninstall

The plugin can remove its settings, cache files, configuration files, log files and scheduled events on uninstall if the uninstall cleanup option is enabled before uninstalling.

If uninstall cleanup is not enabled, settings and generated files are left in place so the site owner can remove or inspect them manually.

Generated WebP image files are not automatically removed unless the plugin uninstall cleanup process specifically handles them. This helps avoid removing media files that may still be referenced by the site.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it from the WordPress plugin screen.
  2. Activate Holographic Extreme Cache.
  3. Open Holo-Cache in the admin menu.
  4. Enable caching from the Dashboard or Cache tab.
  5. Use the Setup tab to check WP_CACHE, cache delivery, helper options and the setup checklist.
  6. Use the Images tab if you want newly uploaded JPEG and PNG images converted to WebP where supported by your server.
  7. Use the homepage speed test to confirm the cache is working.
sections.faq:
What does Holographic Extreme Cache actually do?

Holographic Extreme Cache creates static HTML versions of eligible WordPress pages so they can load faster for visitors. It also includes smart cache clearing, preload support, WooCommerce-aware exclusions, browser cache helper rules, new-upload WebP conversion where supported, speed checks and diagnostics.

Is Holographic Extreme Cache suitable for WooCommerce sites?

Yes. The plugin includes WooCommerce-aware cache rules for cart, checkout, account, order and session behaviour. It is designed to keep dynamic shopping areas safe while still allowing normal public pages and product content to benefit from caching.

Will it clear the right pages when I update content?

Holographic Extreme Cache includes smart cache clearing for common WordPress changes. When content changes, the plugin can clear relevant cached pages instead of forcing you to manually rebuild the whole cache every time.

Does it help rebuild the cache after it has been cleared?

Yes. The plugin includes preload support so important pages can be warmed again after cache clearing. This helps reduce the number of first visitors who hit uncached pages after updates.

Can it convert images to WebP?

Yes, where supported by your server. The free plugin can convert newly uploaded JPEG and PNG images to WebP after the feature is enabled. It keeps the original image files as fallbacks.

Will it convert images that are already in my Media Library?

No. The free plugin only handles new uploads after WebP conversion is enabled. Holographic Extreme Cache Pro can scan and convert images that were uploaded before the feature was enabled, using background processing.

What does my server need for image conversion?

Your hosting environment needs PHP image support that can create WebP files, usually through GD or Imagick. If WebP conversion is not available, the Images tab will show a clear message and page caching will continue to work normally.

How do I know whether the cache is working?

The plugin includes cache diagnostics, response headers, homepage speed testing and health checks. These tools help confirm whether pages are being cached, served correctly and cleared when expected.

Can I exclude pages that should not be cached?

Yes. Holographic Extreme Cache includes exclusion controls for pages and request types that should stay dynamic. This is useful for forms, accounts, carts, checkouts and other areas where fresh or personalised content matters.

Does this cache logged-in users?

Logged-in users are bypassed by default, which is safest for most sites. Advanced users can enable logged-in user caching, but it is not recommended for shops, membership sites, course sites, forums or sites with personalised content unless you fully understand the risks.

Does it include optimisation features beyond page caching?

Yes. The free plugin includes safe HTML minification, WordPress emoji disabling, browser cache helper rules and new-upload WebP conversion where supported. Holographic Extreme Cache Pro adds advanced optimisation features such as existing media conversion, AVIF support where supported, Critical CSS, Cloudflare support, CDN rewriting, per-page optimisation profiles and safer Pro controls.

What is the difference between the free plugin and Pro?

The free plugin focuses on fast static page caching, smart clearing, safe exclusions, preload, diagnostics and new-upload WebP conversion. Pro adds a wider optimisation layer, including existing media image conversion, on-server WebP and AVIF conversion where supported, Critical CSS, advanced preload, Cloudflare, CDN rewriting, Safe Mode, WooCommerce diagnostics, per-page optimisation profiles, performance reports and rollback tools.
sections.changelog:
1.0.49

  • Added an Images tab with optional WebP conversion for newly uploaded JPEG and PNG images where supported by the server.
  • Added server capability checks so image conversion cannot be enabled when WebP generation is unavailable.
  • Added safe WebP fallback handling so original images remain available.
  • Added setup checklist guidance to the Setup tab.
  • Expanded diagnostics with image conversion readiness checks.
  • Updated plugin wording, help text and FAQ entries for the new Images tab.
  • Clarified logged-in user caching behaviour in the FAQ.

1.0.48

  • More dashboard cleanup and simple wording changes.

1.0.47

  • Updated admin screens so main content panels, settings sections, help sections and tables use the available page width.
  • Removed unnecessary dashboard status cards.
  • Changed the disabled-WP-Cron preload fallback so the Cache tab loads first, then processes one safe batch asynchronously.

1.0.46

  • Rebuilt the free plugin help page with clearer sections for setup, dashboard, page cache, preload, optimisation, exclusions, health checks and troubleshooting.

1.0.45

  • Added WP-Cron-disabled preload handling with a clear admin warning, help-page guidance, a sample server cron command, manual safe batch processing and controlled admin-page batch fallback.
  • Updated the setup notice so an authenticated HEC admin action marks setup as handled.

1.0.44

  • Updated the cache speed-check wording.
